source.text: A HÁTAD MÖGÖTT EGY NYERSTEJ-SZÁLLÍTÓ TANKER ÁLL, MINDENT LÁTTAM A FÉNYES FÉMFELÜLETEN VISSZATÜKRÖZVE.
TE VAGY AZ ELSŐ KUTYÁM. EDDIG KAGYLÓIM VOLTAK.

scene.summary: A dog owner tries to play the classic fake-throw stick trick on his dog, pretending he threw the branch high into the air. The unimpressed dog doesn't budge and deadpans a surprisingly articulate explanation: he saw the man hide the stick reflected in the shiny metal tank of a parked raw milk transport truck behind him. Dumbfounded by his pet's intellectual and verbal prowess, the man drops the stick and confesses that this is his very first dog, having only ever kept pet clams before.

characters.name: man in winter coat
characters.description: A man wearing a winter coat, trousers, and a pom-pom knit cap. He plays childish fetch games and speaks in colloquial Hungarian before being stunned into deadpan bewilderment.

characters.name: dog
characters.description: A white pet dog sitting calmly with an unimpressed, half-lidded expression. Contrary to canine expectations, he speaks articulate, formal, technical Hungarian in a deadpan tone.

panels.description: The man in the winter coat playfully waves a twig at his dog, excitedly urging him to play.
Close-up on the sitting dog, looking entirely indifferent and unimpressed.
The man performs the fake-throw trick, hiding the twig behind his back while gazing up and pretending to track its flight in the sky.

Bringing the twig back out, the man remarks that the dog is tough to fool; the dog speaks from off-camera, explaining rationally that he saw the whole trick reflected in a shiny raw milk tanker parked behind the man.
Stunned, the man drops the twig and explains his naivety by admitting he previously only kept pet clams, while the dog responds with a speech bubble containing only a single dot.

notes: The comic parodies the familiar game where dog owners pretend to throw a stick or ball to confuse their pet ('fake throw'). Here, the dog is not tricked at all.

The humor peaks in panel p3 with the dog's unexpectedly formal, precise diction: rather than relying on canine smell or instinct, he rationally deduces the trick using a 'nyerstej-szállító tanker' (raw milk transport tanker truck) as a mirror. The overly specific industrial term creates an absurd contrast with a regular backyard fetch game.

The punchline in panel p4 ('Eddig kagylóim voltak' - 'Until now I had clams/mussels') is absurdly deadpan: clams are sessile, brainless mollusks, making them the most absurd and passive 'pet' possible to contrast with an articulate, hyper-observant dog.
In panel p4, the dog's speech bubble containing a solitary dot ('.') indicates stunned silence, a deadpan pause, or utter wordlessness in response to the owner's admission.

r4.literal: You are not easy to fool,
